findings.issue: The revised PROP-005 grep `grep -inE '\b(if|elif|case)\b.*\b(claude|sonnet|clawrouter|anthropic|blockrun)\b'` is LINE-BASED, so its `case` arm can never match the idiomatic multi-line shell `case` statement, where the scrutinee (`case "$MODEL" in`) is on one line and the model-token arm (`claude) ...`) is on the NEXT line. This is not hypothetical: this very codebase writes exactly that form at clip-cli.sh:22-25 (`case "${1:-}" in` then `  --status)` / `  --restart)` on following lines). A genuine model branch written as `case "$PROVIDER" in / claude) run_x ;; / clawrouter) run_y ;; / esac` — the natural shell construct for multi-way branching on the caller's model — would therefore return ZERO grep hits and pass PROP-005 while flagrantly violating REQ-005. The Gate (verification-architecture.md:39) singles out PROP-005 as the obligation 'most likely to silently regress,' yet its method cannot detect the most idiomatic regression form. Additionally, PROP-005's prose is factually incorrect: it claims 'the pattern only matches inside if/elif/case constructs' and 'path-literal occurrences of .claude/skills/... are out of scope by construction,' but (a) the pattern matches the ENGLISH words 'if'/'case' in comments/prose — proven live at tests/test_instance_paths.sh:17 which the pattern DOES match on 'case ... clawrouter' — and (b) it WOULD match a legitimate `.claude/skills` path literal whenever that literal shares a line with a conditional keyword (e.g. `if [ -d "$HOME/.claude/skills/foo" ]; then`), since `\bclaude\b` matches the `claude` token inside `.claude/skills`. The iteration-2 false positives on the four bare assignments are indeed gone (grep returns zero on producer.sh/run.sh/monitor.sh/_instance_paths.sh), but the method remains unsound in both directions. Fix: make the check line-independent for `case` arms (e.g. also grep for `^[[:space:]]*(claude|sonnet|clawrouter|anthropic|blockrun)\)` as a case-arm label) OR invert the approach — strip known-safe path literals first (`grep -vE '\.claude/skills|\.cloak'`) then do a broad word-boundary token grep — and delete the false 'only matches inside constructs / out of scope by construction' claims.

findings.issue: REQ-005 restricts the model-agnosticism guarantee to `producer.sh/run.sh/monitor.sh/_instance_paths.sh` and asserts 'any calling agent (human-funded Claude Code session, self-funded ClawRouter process, or any future AI) can invoke the same scripts; only env vars differ.' But the actual persistent-loop entrypoint that lives in the SAME skill directory, clip-cli.sh, hardcodes `--model sonnet` (clip-cli.sh:33) and the `claude` binary (clip-cli.sh:15) and dispatches via `case` (clip-cli.sh:22). It is neither in REQ-005's file list nor in PROP-005's grep. The spec's Out-of-scope section (lines 27-33) defers 'provisioning a full second live identity,' but it never states that the loop LAUNCHER is instance/model-specific — so REQ-005's blanket 'only env vars differ' is contradicted by the fact that keeping the loop alive (clip-cli.sh, restarted by the launchd healthcheck referenced at clip-cli.sh:6-7) is Claude+sonnet-only, and a ClawRouter self-funded instance has no agnostic way to run as a persistent service. This lets a Phase 3 reviewer mark REQ-005 PASS while the feature's stated mission ('works for every AI... no human loop') is unmet for the invocation path. Fix: either (a) bring clip-cli.sh into REQ-005's file scope and PROP-005's check (and de-hardcode the model), or (b) add an explicit REQ-005 carve-out clause stating the launcher is instance-specific and out of the agnosticism guarantee, with the ClawRouter launcher named as the follow-on feature — so 'only env vars differ' is scoped to the loop body, not overstated.
